messages:
Jordan: hitting a 400 from tool-call when invoking our user-info tool via function-calls. stack trace says 'tool not found: getUserInfo'.
Maria: ugh. Sorry Jordan — can you paste the request payload and any headers?
Jordan: here's the minimal body we send (from our frontend):
```json
{
  \"name\": \"getUserInfo\",
  \"arguments\": { \"user_id\": \"u-2384\" }
}
```
and the API response is 400 with body:
```json
{
  \"error\": \"tool_not_found\",
  \"message\": \"getUserInfo not available for model rwd-llama-13b-v1\"
}
```
Maria: that message usually means the function registry doesn't contain that exact name. Did you recently rename the tool?
Jordan: nope, this used to work yesterday. We did a small refactor and changed some server-side names but the client still sends getUserInfo. We validated the server has a function named `get_user_info` now.
Sam: tagging infra — @registry-bot any recent registry syncs for the support org?
registry-bot: background sync completed at 2024-12-08T18:12:44Z. 3 entries were updated. No errors reported.
Ingrid: pinging runtime logs for the failed request. Jordan, can you share the exact request id from the 400?
Jordan: request-id: rwd-req-9f3a
Ingrid: grabbing logs...
Ingrid: got it. Runtime log snippet for rwd-req-9f3a:
```
[2024-12-08T18:14:03Z] incoming function_call: name=getUserInfo, model=rwd-llama-13b-v1, user=team-x
[2024-12-08T18:14:03Z] registry lookup -> exact match failed for 'getUserInfo'
[2024-12-08T18:14:03Z] trying aliases: 'get_user_info', 'GetUserInfo', 'getUserinfo'
[2024-12-08T18:14:03Z] alias match found: 'get_user_info' -> bound to tool id tool_827
```
Ingrid: weird, the runtime found an alias and bound to tool_827, but the next message shows an error calling the tool: 
```
[2024-12-08T18:14:03Z] tool invocation failed: tool_827 error: "schema mismatch: expected args {\"user_id\":string} got {\"user\":{\"id\":\"u-2384\"}}"
```
Jordan: our frontend switched to passing a nested `user` object by mistake during that refactor. So two issues: client changed args shape and server changed canonical name (underscore). But the runtime aliasing should have saved us.
Maria: right — aliasing caught the name, but schema validation failed. We need to confirm which change caused production break: the name change should be safe; schema change isn't.
Sam: registry shows tool_827 schema is still {"user_id": "string"}. The last registry update from the customer's repo had a new interface with nested `user`. Likely the customer's deploy updated their internal function config but registry sync didn't pick up the new schema for this model/tenant.
Ingrid: I see an inconsistency: registry service has two versions: canonical tool name `get_user_info` v1 (user_id string) and a newer alias admin pushed as `GetUserInfo` v2 (user: { id:string }). registry-bot logs show v2 was pushed but not promoted to model binding for rwd-llama-13b-v1 due to a failed sync step.
registry-bot: sync failed on 2024-12-08T17:59:12Z for org team-x: error=etag-mismatch; attempted rolls: 1
Sam: there we go. So runtime aliasing matched to the canonical v1, but the customer's frontend expects v2. That explains the schema mismatch.
Maria: action items: Jordan — revert client to send {"user_id": "..."} as quick mitigation. Sam/Ingrid — investigate why registry sync returned etag-mismatch and re-run.
Jordan: reverting client now, ETA 10m.
Jordan: update — rolled back frontend to user_id payload, confirmed successful calls (no 400) at 18:22.
Ingrid: I'm re-triggering a manual registry sync for team-x and forcing a full compare.
registry-bot: manual sync started for team-x by Ingrid at 2024-12-08T18:24:10Z
registry-bot: manual sync completed at 2024-12-08T18:25:03Z. Result: merged v2 into model binding for rwd-llama-13b-v1; no conflicts.
Ingrid: after merge, I kicked a light rollout to canary nodes.
deploy-bot: canary rollout to 5 nodes started for registry binding update at 2024-12-08T18:26:00Z
deploy-bot: canary rollout succeeded at 2024-12-08T18:28:10Z
Jordan: re-testing client with new nested `user` body — works now. Thanks!
Maria: I left a short postmortem template in the ticket. Summary for support case: root cause was registry sync etag-mismatch causing model binding to remain on older tool schema; aliasing prevented immediate name-based failure, but schema mismatch caused 400s.
Sam: will add an alert on registry sync etag-mismatch and add a spec check that rejects alias matches if schemas differ by major shape without explicit opt-in.
Ingrid: will also publish a KB: "Tool name aliases vs schema drift" with recommended client best-practices (version pinning + graceful fallback) and an operator playbook for registry sync failure.
Jordan: appreciated. Marking resolved from customer side. :white_check_mark:
Maria: closing thread but leaving notes for follow-ups on infra/registry tickets. :slightly_smiling_face:
